aluxVsOthers.universal.text.source: ALUX models parallel, concurrent, and composite transition patterns beyond one-shot state updates.

aluxVsOthers.what.items.0.1.source: Most chains optimize ordered state updates. ALUX gives decentralized services a runtime that stays alive across time.

aluxVsOthers.what.items.1.1.source: Processes can interleave, suspend, resume, and coordinate through tuple-space messaging instead of forcing every workflow into one block.

aluxVsOthers.what.items.2.1.source: OCAP-style references make authority explicit and unforgeable, so processes can pass and attenuate what they are allowed to do.

aluxVsOthers.what.text.source: ALUX is the layer between execution, permissions, commit logic, and consensus. It lets smart contracts and agents pause, wait, resume, coordinate, and carry scoped authority across trust boundaries.

glvm.architecture.layers.2.text.source: The machines that do the work. Public-chain nodes provide the current execution foundation. Private or cloud TVMs are the next integration surface; client-device TVMs remain a roadmap path toward local execution.

glvm.architecture.text.source: Physical machines run TVMs; in the GLVM architecture, those engines participate in one shared logical execution model. A future World OS will organize that layer into discoverable, orchestrated services governed by explicit capabilities.

glvm.continuity.atomicity.title.source: Cross-block execution preserves one transaction context.

glvm.continuity.modes.1.text.source: Independent transitions advance at the same time.

glvm.continuity.modes.2.text.source: Processes communicate, wait, and resume through channels.

glvm.continuity.modes.3.text.source: Multiple concurrent transactions share a higher-level atomic objective.

glvm.continuity.notes.0.text.source: Concurrent TVM execution · COMM wait and resume · ReplayTrie · cross-block continuation and finalization

glvm.continuity.notes.1.text.source: Tentative intermediate state does not become confirmed state until finalization; a failed path is discarded instead of repaired later through compensating transactions.

glvm.continuity.notes.2.text.source: An authenticated HTTPS GET can suspend, record the response, replay, and resume. The data source still determines truth, and irreversible off-chain side effects remain outside rollback.

glvm.continuity.notes.3.text.source: Cross-shard atomic execution and composition with independent external systems define the next expansion of the model.

glvm.continuity.steps.0.text.source: Start one transaction with one scoped set of capabilities.

glvm.continuity.steps.1.text.source: If an answer or channel match is missing, preserve the continuation instead of finalizing early.

glvm.continuity.steps.2.text.source: ReplayTrie records the non-deterministic choice or authenticated response required to reproduce the path.

glvm.continuity.steps.3.text.source: A matching COMM event or recorded response wakes the preserved continuation in a later block.

glvm.continuity.steps.4.text.source: At the finalization boundary, eligible state is committed; rejected tentative state is discarded.

glvm.continuity.text.source: Execution evolves from sequential and parallel work to concurrent processes that communicate, wait, and resume. Composite execution extends the model so multiple concurrent transactions can share a higher-level settlement boundary; cross-block continuity provides the vertical foundation for that direction.

glvm.continuity.title.source: A transaction can wait across blocks, then settle as one

glvm.definition.comparison.0.note.source: One concrete engine inside a machine

glvm.definition.comparison.0.text.source: The concrete ALUX execution engine. It runs Tolang bytecode, coordinates independent processes through channels and COMM events, and records the non-deterministic choices required for deterministic replay.

glvm.definition.comparison.1.note.source: One logical system above many machines

glvm.definition.comparison.1.text.source: GLVM defines the developer-facing logical model across participating TVMs. It provides one boundary for execution state and processes while replay, replication, finalization, and consensus remain beneath the abstraction.

glvm.definition.payoff.text.source: Developers target one concurrent execution model while the runtime handles scheduling, replay, capability checks, replication, and finalization.

glvm.definition.payoff.title.source: One logical execution layer, not one physical machine

glvm.definition.text.source: TVM is the bytecode execution engine on one machine. GLVM defines the system-level execution abstraction across participating TVMs. It is not another bytecode VM; developers target one logical model while deterministic replay, execution continuity, replication, finalization, and consensus are coordinated beneath the abstraction.

glvm.definition.title.source: One TVM per machine, coordinated through one logical execution model

glvm.hero.text.source: GLVM is the developer-facing execution abstraction ALUX is building from its concurrent runtime. A TVM provides the concrete engine on each participating machine; the GLVM model brings execution state, processes, replay, replication, and consensus into one logical layer.

glvm.ocapStory.alt.source: A CEO and Bob meet; the identity badge on the left represents broad access, while one OCAP key on the right names only Bob’s record.

glvm.ocapStory.boundary.text.source: Here, “key” visually represents an OCAP unforgeable name—a capability reference. It is not a cryptographic key. This guarantee applies to TVM-native, capability-mediated interactions; hosted EVM permissions and external services need their own controls.

glvm.ocapStory.caption.source: CEO + Bob · OCAP key = unforgeable name, not a cryptographic key

glvm.ocapStory.comparison.0.text.source: Even when the task concerns Bob alone, the identity authority represented by the CEO’s badge can still cover Financials and the records of Alice, Carol, and Bob.

glvm.ocapStory.comparison.0.title.source: The badge carries unrelated access into the task

glvm.ocapStory.comparison.1.text.source: This key represents an unforgeable name that identifies Bob’s record. Without a capability reference to another pre-existing object, the task cannot name or reach it. The TVM checks that boundary at runtime.

glvm.ocapStory.comparison.1.title.source: The task receives one key that names Bob’s record

glvm.ocapStory.takeaway.text.source: Model safeguards can reduce unsafe behavior, but capability boundaries enforce least authority at runtime. If an agent has only the key that names Bob’s record, compromise stays within that object instead of expanding to all the identity authority represented by the CEO’s badge.

glvm.ocapStory.text.source: In the CEO–Bob example, identity-based access can carry the ambient authority represented by the CEO’s badge into the task. With object capabilities, the task receives only one key that names Bob’s record. The TVM enforces the reachable boundary at runtime. Without a capability reference to another pre-existing object, the task cannot name or reach it.

glvm.ocapStory.title.source: Give the task one key—not the user’s badge

glvm.stack.items.0.text.source: The concrete concurrent engine runs bytecode and lets independent processes exchange data and continuations through channels.

glvm.stack.items.1.text.source: Unforgeable references make reachable authority explicit and let the runtime enforce least-authority boundaries.

glvm.stack.items.2.text.source: Execution contexts can suspend across blocks, resume from preserved continuations, and reach a deferred finalization boundary.

glvm.stack.items.3.text.source: A block DAG, deterministic leader rotation, and merge rules converge concurrent chain-side work without a permanent leader.

glvm.stack.items.4.text.source: Recorded non-deterministic choices and execution traces let validators reproduce the accepted path.

glvm.stack.items.5.text.source: The node layer carries proposals, blocks, state evidence, and validator coordination beneath the execution abstraction.

glvm.stack.items.6.text.source: Tolang describes concurrent processes; the compiler lowers source into TVM-executable bytecode.

glvm.stack.items.7.text.source: The EVM runs as a stateful guest through TSAC-style coordination. WASM extends the heterogeneous-VM direction.

glvm.stack.items.8.text.source: The compiler, LSP, playground, test suite, and diagnostics bring the execution model into developer workflows.

glvm.stack.text.source: GLVM is not a second bytecode VM. These nine architecture views—from TVM execution, object capabilities, and replay to BlockGit, guest VMs, and developer tooling—show the capability system behind its logical execution model.

home.hero.text.source: Imagine one logical virtual machine that runs everywhere—across public blockchains, private clusters, and client environments such as phones and browsers—while abstracting the underlying state, threads, replication, and consensus. Developers write one concurrent program; where it runs becomes a configuration choice rather than an architectural constraint. Its parts still commit together as one atomic result. That is Virtual Machine Abstraction, and ALUX is building it.

home.sections.2.clusters.0.detailTechnic.source: TVM bytecode processes communicate through typed tuple-space channels. They can wait on input, resume later, and keep their execution context.

home.sections.2.clusters.0.runtimeBusine.source: This lets ALUX run live services rather than only one-shot transactions.

home.sections.2.clusters.0.runtimeTechni.source: Tolang compiles into TVM bytecode. Processes fork, wait, resume, and communicate through typed tuple-space channels without shared memory.

home.sections.2.clusters.0.text.source: The Tuple-Space Virtual Machine executes bytecode processes that fork, wait, resume, and communicate through typed channels.

home.sections.2.clusters.1.detailBusines.source: Each task receives only the capabilities it needs; authority unrelated to the task never enters its execution context.

home.sections.2.clusters.1.detailTechnic.source: OCAP represents authority as unforgeable channel references. A process can use only references it created or was explicitly passed; capabilities can then be attenuated and constrained by channel usage and lifecycle rules.

home.sections.2.clusters.1.runtimeBusine.source: Prompt injection may influence a process, but it cannot invoke capabilities that were never passed into that process.

home.sections.2.clusters.1.runtimeTechni.source: OCAP channel references are unforgeable. Each process starts only with capabilities explicitly introduced into its environment; namespaces, attenuation, and lifecycle rules narrow what each holder can do.

home.sections.2.clusters.2.runtimeTechni.source: Segments, partitions, ReplayTrie, isolation, and commit rules preserve one transaction across suspension and later-block resumption.

home.sections.2.clusters.9.runtimeBusine.source: Horizontal scale should not force applications to recover from half-completed shard interactions.

home.sections.2.clusters.9.runtimeTechni.source: The design requires all participating shard-local effects to commit together or abort together, while tentative intermediate state remains unobservable. Cross-shard execution remains on the roadmap.

home.sections.2.clusters.9.text.source: Design target: extend the same all-or-nothing transaction boundary across shards. Every shard-local effect commits together or none does, and unrelated transactions should never observe a partial cross-shard result.

home.sections.6.items.0.1.source: A workflow starts several agents in parallel. Some call the Claude API, while other steps wait for user input. The main agent continues only after every branch finishes, even when the workflow runs for about 30 minutes. Claude and user input connect at the application layer; ALUX provides durable fork, wait, join, capability passing, and replayable execution.

home.sections.6.items.1.0.source: BTC Price Aggregation from Three Exchanges

home.sections.6.items.1.1.source: A contract starts three parallel processes through configured external-I/O adapters to read BTC prices from Binance, Coinbase, and Kraken. A fourth process waits for all three, joins their results, normalizes the quotes, computes the median, and then continues. ALUX makes the execution reproducible; the selected endpoints still determine source truth.

home.sections.6.items.2.1.source: Contract a on Shard A stages payment for a ticket managed by contract b on Shard B. If b fails because the ticket is already sold, a's payment is rolled back. Only when both steps succeed do payment and ticket ownership commit together; other transactions see neither partial state. Cross-shard atomic execution is a roadmap target, not a live capability today.

home.sections.6.items.3.1.source: Alice gives Bob a purse containing 1 ALUX and adds a rule: the funds must be used within 10 days. When Bob gives the same purse to Carole, he adds a second rule: it may be used only to buy books. Carole must satisfy both rules, and passing the purse does not duplicate the funds. The time limit and spending rule are enforced by application logic.

home.sections.9.items.0.0.source: Is ALUX just another faster L1?

home.sections.9.items.0.1.source: No. Faster L1s accelerate the same abstraction: one-shot state updates that happen within one block. ALUX is a decentralized concurrent runtime for Long Transactions that can wait, resume, join across multiple channels, or select whichever channel becomes ready first; their state updates are no longer constrained by a block boundary. Through its GLVM architecture—Virtual Machine Abstraction—the same logical transaction is designed to extend beyond block boundaries toward shard and system boundaries.

home.sections.9.items.1.0.source: What becomes possible on ALUX that ordinary smart contracts cannot do?

home.sections.9.items.1.1.source: ALUX extends the smart-contract model into a decentralized durable execution engine for long-running jobs. A workflow can run concurrent processes, suspend across blocks, wait for external tools or people, resume, and join results without exposing half-completed state. Runtime-mediated external channels can interact with supported off-chain services without separate oracle-and-relayer choreography. The architecture is designed to extend the same atomic model horizontally, so cross-shard effects commit or abort together; cross-shard execution remains on the roadmap.

home.sections.9.items.2.0.source: Why is ALUX built for AI agents?

home.sections.9.items.2.1.source: An on-chain agent is naturally a Long Transaction. Calling an LLM or a tool takes time; waiting for a human response also takes time. The workflow cannot be forced into an instant, one-block call. ALUX lets it preserve execution context, suspend, resume when inputs arrive, coordinate concurrent agents, and finalize through replayable execution.

home.sections.9.items.3.1.source: Object Capability (OCAP) is a security model where the only way a piece of code can access a resource is by being explicitly given a reference (a capability) to that resource. In an OCAP system, the same object reference both identifies a resource (designation) and grants permission to use it (authorization).

home.sections.9.items.4.0.source: How does ALUX keep Long Transactions deterministic?

home.sections.9.items.4.1.source: ReplayTrie records the non-deterministic COMM choices that affect execution, enabling bit-exact deterministic replay inside the ALUX runtime so validators can reproduce the same execution outcome.

home.sections.9.items.5.0.source: Can existing smart contract developers use it?

home.sections.9.items.5.1.source: TVM runs EVM bytecode inside isolated sandboxes, so most EVM contracts can be migrated to ALUX with minimal changes. ALUX also presents an Ethereum-compatible view through a set of commonly used eth_* JSON-RPC methods.

home.sections.9.items.6.0.source: Some other chains also claim to support cross-block transactions. How is ALUX different?

home.sections.9.items.6.1.source:
The keyword is atomicity.

Compensation / Saga: commit → commit → ✗ fail → run compensating undo
Each step commits locally, intermediate states are visible, compensation can also fail, and external effects cannot always be reversed. This is eventual consistency. Some asynchronous chains, including ICP and Rialo, lean on this model. It is easier to implement, but unsuitable for applications that require stronger ACID guarantees.

ALUX all-or-nothing: stage → stage → ✗ fail → discard everything
Nothing commits until the whole transaction commits. On abort, uncommitted effects are discarded and no partial state becomes observable. That is true ACID atomicity across block heights.

home.sections.9.items.7.0.source: Why is OCAP a stronger and composable security model?

home.sections.9.items.7.1.source: Object Capability (OCAP) is a stronger security model because authority is represented by explicit, unforgeable capabilities rather than global identities or access control lists. It follows the principle that designation is authorization: possessing a capability both identifies a resource and grants permission to use it, eliminating ambient authority and reducing the attack surface. Because capabilities can be safely delegated, attenuated, and revoked, security policies become local to the objects involved instead of being scattered across a centralized permission system. This makes OCAP naturally composable, allowing complex applications, smart contracts, and AI agent workflows to be built from independently secure components while preserving the principle of least privilege.

home.sections.9.items.8.0.source: What does it mean for OCAP to be natively supported in ALUX?

home.sections.9.items.8.1.source: ALUX’s Tuple-Space Virtual Machine (TVM) implements the Object Capability (OCAP) model directly at the bytecode level. The instruction set contains no operations for forging or constructing arbitrary object references, ensuring that capabilities can only be acquired through explicit delegation. This guarantees that all authority is both unforgeable and explicitly transferred.

parallelConcurrentComposable.close.point.source: More throughput, but no transaction dependency or message matching.
Transactions can interact and wait, but cross-system effects may still settle separately.
An atomic boundary exists, but without interaction and waiting it cannot carry long-running dependencies.

parallelConcurrentComposable.close.text.source: Parallelism handles independent execution. Concurrency handles message-driven interaction and wait/resume. ALUX implements those runtime foundations today and is building toward atomic composition across system boundaries.

parallelConcurrentComposable.foundations.source: A process can fork, wait in one block, and resume in a later block without restarting its local execution context.
A waiting consume meets another transaction's produce. The match activates the continuation while unrelated work keeps moving.
Unforgeable capability references are passed explicitly, so each step receives only the authority it needs; identity does not automatically bring unrelated authority into scope.
Only the non-deterministic COMM choices that matter are recorded, so validators can reproduce the same execution.
Concurrent work enters verified fringes, where overlaps are classified as accepted, rejected, or undecided before finality.
A long-running service stays coherent because every step can run, interact, carry explicit authority, replay deterministically, and settle along one verifiable atomic path.

GLVM describes the broader architecture for extending that logical model across blockchain nodes, cloud services, and personal devices.
One logical runtime across many environments

parallelConcurrentComposable.hero.text.source: ALUX supports replayable long transactions: independent tasks run together and transactions coordinate through messages. The booking scenario illustrates the target model for settling related cross-system effects as one atomic result.

parallelConcurrentComposable.hero.visual.source: A premium technical illustration of the ALUX runtime connecting nodes, cloud services, devices, agents, capability tokens, and commit rails.

parallelConcurrentComposable.intro.claim.source: In the current ALUX runtime, independent work can run in parallel, transactions coordinate through messages, and execution can resume across blocks. Atomic composition across independent systems remains an architecture target.

parallelConcurrentComposable.intro.text.source: Parallel runs independent transactions at the same time. Concurrency lets transactions interact through channels: one transaction can wait for a matching message from another, then continue. Composability binds state transitions from different systems into one auditable atomic transition.

parallelConcurrentComposable.intro.title.source: Three words, three very different runtime jobs

parallelConcurrentComposable.lab.benefit.source: Independent work does not wait behind one global queue.
The dependency lives in a channel instead of blocking the runtime.
The booking waits for the hotel
The COMM creates the continuation; ReplayTrie records the choice only when the match is non-deterministic.
The reply creates the next step
The target is one all-or-nothing result with reproducible settlement evidence.

parallelConcurrentComposable.lab.message.source: Start with step 1. Reservation and payment are managed separately inside the same runtime.
Parallel: reservation and payment checks advance at the same time without sharing state.
Concurrent wait: the reservation leaves a room-availability condition in the channel; payment work can keep moving.
Message matched: the hotel replies with availability. ALUX activates the booking continuation; if several matches were possible, ReplayTrie fixes the chosen one.
Composition target: the room hold and payment authorization close together as one all-or-nothing booking result.

parallelConcurrentComposable.lab.steps.0.source: Reservation and payment checks advance independently.

parallelConcurrentComposable.lab.steps.1.source: The reservation leaves an availability condition in the channel.

parallelConcurrentComposable.lab.steps.2.source: The matching message activates the booking continuation.

parallelConcurrentComposable.lab.steps.3.source: Room hold and payment authorization commit as one result.

parallelConcurrentComposable.lab.text.source: Use four actions to explore the target composition model: start reservation and payment checks, leave a room-availability wait, deliver the hotel's matching message, then model a joint confirmation.

parallelConcurrentComposable.metaDescrip.source: A visual guide to ALUX's current parallel and message-driven execution, plus its target model for atomic composition across system boundaries.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.0.alt.source: Multiple isolated execution rails moving forward at the same time.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.0.con.source: Parallelism finds several answers at once. It does not make those jobs interact.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.0.ena.source: More independent work finishes in the same amount of time. But parallelism alone cannot make those jobs exchange messages or let a long transaction wait and continue.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.0.how.source: Parallel execution is native to ALUX's process calculus: transactions share no memory, and any interaction is confined to tuple-space channels. Independent transactions therefore advance in separate TVM lanes, while Block Merge resolves state overlap at commit time.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.0.tit.source:
Flight, hotel, transfer, and insurance
search at the same time

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.0.wha.source: Parallel execution means independent jobs run at the same time. A travel agent can search flights, rooms, transfers, and insurance without making one search wait behind another.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.1.alt.source: Two transactions interact through a tuple-space channel: one waits for a matching message, the other sends it, and the waiting continuation resumes while unrelated work keeps moving.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.1.con.source: Concurrency turns a reply into the next step: the match creates a new continuation instead of merely restarting a stopped lane.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.1.cue.source: The booking waits; a hotel agent replies; the next step begins

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.1.ena.source: A travel agent can keep one long transaction alive across blocks: it waits for room availability, an API response, or a user decision, then continues without blocking unrelated work.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.1.how.source: The waiting consume is stored as a resource in tuple space. A produce from another transaction matches it, triggering a COMM event that spawns the continuation and moves the Execution Context from Inactive back to Running. If more than one match is possible, ReplayTrie records the chosen COMM for deterministic replay.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.1.tit.source:
A booking waits for availability
and continues when the reply arrives

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.1.wha.source: Concurrency begins when jobs interact. A booking can leave a waiting condition in a channel, and a hotel service can satisfy it later by sending the matching availability message.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.2.alt.source: A room reservation and payment authorization arrive from different systems. Only after both are ready does one booking confirmation leave the atomic boundary.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.2.con.source: The target composition model gives different systems one all-or-nothing result; concurrency carries the messages that lead up to that shared commit.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.2.cue.source: The booking confirms only when reservation and payment both succeed

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.2.ena.source: The intended result is to avoid a half-finished booking such as money charged without a room, or a room held without payment.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.2.how.source: The current runtime provides tuple-space coordination, scoped OCAP references, cross-block continuation, ReplayTrie, and Block Merge. End-to-end atomic composition across independent external systems remains a design target built from those primitives.

parallelConcurrentComposable.modes.2.wha.source: Composition is not ordinary bundling. The target in this example is to commit the room hold and payment authorization together, or commit neither one.

team.metaDescription.source: Meet the lead developers building ALUX's concurrent runtime, language, consensus, and blockchain systems stack.

team.sections.0.items.0.bio.0.source: Frank is a concurrent systems architect. Before ALUX, he spent nearly 20 years at Lehman Brothers, Barclays Capital, and Bloomberg as a senior quant and derivatives engineer, building Wall Street-grade risk systems that had to stay correct under concurrency — across time zones, organizations, and milliseconds.

team.sections.0.items.0.bio.1.source: That career left him with one conviction: the synchronous execution model has reached its end. ALUX is his answer. He led the design of its core stack:

team.sections.0.items.0.closing.0.source: Virtual machine, language, and consensus interlock into one system where concurrent execution and composability finally hold together — a protocol layer built for an open, composable economy of AI agents.

team.sections.0.items.0.highlights.0.1.source: Processes interact concurrently through channels; pattern matching is scheduling; capability credentials are authorization.

team.sections.0.items.0.highlights.1.1.source: Tolang encodes channel descriptors and behavioral types so some misuse can be caught early, while the runtime enforces lifecycle constraints.

team.sections.0.items.0.highlights.2.1.source: A channel reference is unforgeable and transferable; scope and lifecycle rules limit authority without relying on address-based access alone.

team.sections.0.items.0.highlights.3.1.source: Validators produce DAG blocks concurrently. BlockGit uses rotating leader selection for finality, while Block Merge resolves overlapping work.

team.sections.0.items.0.highlights.4.1.source: Segments, rollback, isolation rules, and commit points preserve ACID semantics for long-running and cross-block work.

team.sections.0.items.1.bio.0.source: Tomislav's path into computing started early: a cardboard calculator at five, assembly on a C64c by ten. A decade in electronics and two more as a polyglot programmer — from JavaScript to Haskell — taught him to think from the metal up.

team.sections.0.items.1.bio.1.source: At ALUX he works where theory meets the runtime: using process calculus to make concurrency a first-class citizen, not an afterthought.

team.sections.0.items.2.bio.0.source: Tom is a blockchain developer focused on consensus protocol research — at ALUX, that means BlockGit, the DAG consensus design that lets validators produce blocks concurrently without a permanent leader.

team.sections.0.items.2.bio.1.source: Before ALUX he spent about ten years in the IPC industry, owning system architecture and shipping across DApps, mobile, cloud, web, and desktop — a range that now spans a dozen languages, from C and C++ to Solidity and Rust.

vs.sections.0.statement.source: The capability runtime for production AI agents.

vs.sections.0.text.source: AI agents stop being simple calls once they enter production. They wait for APIs and people, coordinate with other agents, carry scoped authority, and need a record of what happened. ALUX gives that work a decentralized service runtime.

vs.sections.0.title.source: The Runtime Platform forPersistent AI Agents

vs.sections.0.visual.stages.0.1.source: A user, app, or agent starts with scoped purpose.

vs.sections.0.visual.stages.1.1.source: The runtime passes explicit authority instead of raw credentials.

vs.sections.0.visual.stages.2.1.source: Subtasks branch across agents, services, and systems.

vs.sections.0.visual.stages.3.1.source: Execution can pause for APIs, people, timers, or payments.

vs.sections.0.visual.stages.4.1.source: Non-deterministic matches leave a record validators can reproduce.

vs.sections.0.visual.title.source: One lifecycle, not a brittle call chain

vs.sections.1.figure.text.source: A runtime where agents wait, collaborate, carry rights, and remain accountable.

vs.sections.1.items.0.points.2.source: A foundation for scoped tool access

vs.sections.1.items.0.text.source: Authority is carried by unforgeable channel references: what a process may access, invoke, pass onward, or attenuate.

vs.sections.1.items.1.points.0.source: Tuple space messaging for async coordination

vs.sections.1.items.1.text.source: Agent work is collaborative. ALUX supports multi-agent concurrency, async coordination, and workflows that continue across time.

vs.sections.1.items.2.points.2.source: A foundation for governance and safety layers

vs.sections.1.items.2.text.source: ReplayTrie records non-deterministic COMM choices for bit-exact deterministic replay inside the ALUX runtime; committed state transitions provide a foundation for higher-level audit and governance.

vs.sections.1.outro.source: ALUX is not just AI on-chain. It is infrastructure for agent permissions, coordination, and traceable accountability.

vs.sections.1.text.source: Once agent work can actually stay alive, ALUX gives it three platform layers: permissions, coordination, and accountability.

vs.sections.2.closing.source: ALUX gives agent work a full lifecycle: scoped entry, concurrent execution, external waiting, cross-block continuation, and durable record.

vs.sections.2.steps.0.text.source: Work starts with a request, delegated capability, or user intent. The runtime begins with explicit scope and context.

vs.sections.2.steps.1.text.source: Subtasks fan out across agents and services instead of squeezing through one linear path.

vs.sections.2.steps.2.points.1.source: Wait state stays in the runtime

vs.sections.2.steps.2.text.source: Execution can pause for APIs, people, timers, payments, or other real-world events.

vs.sections.2.steps.3.text.source: When the world responds, the workflow continues in a later block with state, memory, and permissions intact.

vs.sections.2.steps.4.points.0.source: Validators reproduce the same recorded execution outcome

vs.sections.2.steps.4.points.1.source: A foundation for governance and trust layers

vs.sections.2.steps.4.text.source: Recorded COMM choices and committed state transitions remain reproducible to validators and available to higher-level audit systems.

vs.sections.2.text.source: An agent workflow does not need to collapse into one bounded call. It can enter with capability scope, branch into concurrent work, suspend at external waits, resume in a later block, and leave an accountable record.

vs.sections.2.title.source: How Agent Work Lives on ALUX

vs.sections.3.closing.source: Together, they keep continuity, coordination, and authority inside the runtime instead of rebuilding them in application code.

vs.sections.3.features.0.text.source: A transaction can suspend at a seam and resume in a later block when its dependencies resolve.

vs.sections.3.features.1.text.source: A process can use only references it created or was explicitly passed; arbitrary authority cannot be forged by an opcode.

vs.sections.3.features.2.text.source: Processes communicate through produce and consume channels. Unmatched work waits; non-deterministic matches are recorded for replay.

vs.sections.3.features.3.text.source: EVM sandboxes keep sequential execution while SLOAD, SSTORE, and CALL reach shared resources through Tuple-space Adapter Contracts.

vs.sections.3.statement.source: Four core mechanisms make long-running agent work native to the platform.

vs.sections.3.text.source: ALUX brings persistent execution, concurrent coordination, explicit authority, and EVM compatibility together in one runtime layer.

vs.sections.4.statement.source: Production-grade agents must be RISC. ALUX builds the machine.

vs.sections.4.systems.0.text.source: Cross-block context preservation and deterministic replay keep long-running work reproducible as it resumes.

vs.sections.4.systems.1.text.source: Reasoning loops, memory, tool use, and task orchestration are where most agent frameworks compete today.

vs.sections.4.systems.2.text.source: Object capabilities, lifecycle constraints, rollback paths, and replay evidence limit which effects a process can attempt and make committed outcomes easier to examine.

vs.sections.4.systems.3.text.source: Designed session-type protocols give agents from different organizations a path to work together without remaining in private silos.

vs.sections.4.text.source: Production-grade agents need a body, a brain, an immune system, and a social layer. Intelligence is only one part of the machine; the runtime must keep work alive, contain risk, and connect work across organizations.

vs.sections.4.title.source: Agents Need MoreThan a Brain
